messages:
Ava (PM): Quick sync — we need to lock MVP scope for the embeddings endpoint this week. major tradeoffs: default dimension support vs. larger batch sizes. who has bandwidth to call this?
Diego (Eng): I can drive. prefer to pick a constrained MVP: fixed dims per model, batch size cap 512. simpler to implement and tests faster.
Samira (ML): Agree on fixed dims per model for MVP. customers expect stable vector shapes (esp. downstream indexes).
Ethan (Platform): 512 seems reasonable but we should validate memory pressure on 4xA100 pools. if we push 512 for 1536-dim vectors it's okay, but 3072 dims -> OOM unless we auto-slice.
Liam (CS): We have 2 pilot customers asking for 3072 dims + 1 big enterprise that needs bulk-ingest 100k docs/day. batching & bulk API matter to them.
Ava (PM): Notes: prioritize predictability for early customers. proposal: MVP = support 1536 (default), 3072 as opt-in model; per-request model selection allowed; limit per-request items to 512; provide a bulk async ingest path for >512.
Diego (Eng): Implementation notes: API shape as POST /v1/embeddings with body {model, input:[...], options:{batch_size}}. server side we still chunk >batch_size into sub-batches. return should include per-item metadata so callers can reconcile ordering.
Samira (ML): Also need to return model_dim in response. many infra pipelines currently rely on shape sanity-check. Suggest response: {model:..., model_dim:1536, data:[{id:..., embedding:[...]}], request_id:...}.
Ethan (Platform): +1 to model_dim. we should also include a header X-Redwood-Processing-Time and a cost_estimate field for predictable unit pricing.
Diego (Eng): For batching: we'll accept a user-supplied batch_hint but cap at 512. server does adaptive slicing based on model dim and available GPU memory. fallback path: if GPU memory insufficient, fallback to smaller slices and include a processing_warning in the response.
Liam (CS): For customers: document that 3072 dims will have higher latency/cost and advise using embeddings.optimize suggestions.
Ava (PM): Launch criteria checklist draft: 1) API contract docs + example code 2) SDK changes (py/ts) 3) perf matrix for 1536 and 3072 (latency, p95, cost/tokens) 4) bulk async path + import tool 5) e2e tests with ordering guarantees 6) migration guide for existing customers.
Diego (Eng): Timeline: 2 weeks for core impl (chunking + response format) + 1 week for perf regression and SDK. can scope down if we drop immediate 3072 rollout.
Samira (ML): Risk: model selection. Recommend we ship with two verified models: rwd-embed-1536-v1 and rwd-embed-3072-v1 (3072 gated). we can add auto-quantized versions later.
Ethan (Platform): Ops: add a per-model mem profile mapping and a protective circuit-breaker that rejects single requests >10k vectors.
Ava (PM): Decision for MVP: ship with 1536 default, allow model param to pick 3072 but marked beta, per-request cap 512, provide bulk async for large loads, response includes model & model_dim + per-item id. Any objections?
Diego (Eng): no objections. I'll open tasks and break down.
Samira (ML): no objections. I'll validate embeddings quality tests for both dims.
Liam (CS): fine. I'll prep customer comms.
CI Bot: created ticket PROD-embeddings-mvp-171842 for tracking :white_check_mark:
Ava (PM): I'll update the roadmap slice and put this as Q2 deliverable. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
